questions.prompt: A temperature feature has different typical values at mountain and coastal stations. Which missing-value strategy best respects this structure when enough training observations exist in each group?

choices.text: Compute group medians using the complete training and test datasets.
Drop every station that has ever reported a missing temperature.
Replace every missing temperature with zero.
Estimate a median within each training-data station group and define a fallback for unseen groups.

questions.explanation: A justified group-specific statistic can preserve differences that a single global value would hide. Estimate the statistics from training data and define how to handle groups with insufficient observations.
questions.answerText: Estimate a median within each training-data station group and define a fallback for unseen groups.

questions.prompt: A KNN model uses income measured in thousands and a ratio ranging from 0 to 1. Why might StandardScaler be useful before fitting?

choices.text: It converts numerical features into class labels.
It removes all outliers without changing other observations.
It reduces the chance that a feature dominates distance mainly because of its numerical scale.
It guarantees that all features have equal predictive value.

questions.explanation: KNN measures proximity using feature values, so measurement scale can strongly influence its neighbors. Standardization adjusts each nonconstant feature using a mean and scale learned from training data.
questions.answerText: It reduces the chance that a feature dominates distance mainly because of its numerical scale.

questions.prompt: Training produces columns color_blue and color_red, but a separately encoded inference batch produces color_red and color_blue in the opposite order. What must the inference workflow do?

choices.text: Apply the fitted encoder and preserve the training feature names and order.
Sort each row's numerical values from smallest to largest.
Pass the inference columns directly because their count is unchanged.
Refit the classifier on the inference batch without labels.

questions.explanation: A model associates each input position with a particular feature meaning. Reusing the fitted encoder maintains a consistent representation across training and inference.
questions.answerText: Apply the fitted encoder and preserve the training feature names and order.

questions.prompt: Which entry belongs in a useful data dictionary for a sensor dataset?

choices.text: Only a screenshot of the first five rows.
A guarantee that all future observations will have the same distribution.
Each field's meaning, unit, type, valid range, and missing-value convention.
Only the final model's accuracy.

questions.explanation: A data dictionary makes feature interpretation and validation explicit. Units and missing-value conventions prevent silent errors such as treating an error code as a real measurement.
questions.answerText: Each field's meaning, unit, type, valid range, and missing-value convention.

questions.prompt: A model predicts machine failure at 08:00. Which candidate feature violates the prediction moment?

choices.text: The machine type recorded during installation.
The previous day's average vibration.
A technician's repair outcome entered at 17:00 after the failure.
The machine's age at 08:00.

questions.explanation: A valid predictor must be available when the prediction is made. A later repair outcome exposes information from after the event and produces an unrealistic evaluation.
questions.answerText: A technician's repair outcome entered at 17:00 after the failure.

questions.prompt: For an ordinary independent binary-classification dataset with a rare positive class, what is the main purpose of a stratified hold-out split?

choices.text: Approximately preserve the original class proportions in each split.
Guarantee the same score in every validation fold.
Make training and test observations identical.
Balance the dataset by discarding all majority-class observations.

questions.explanation: Stratification helps ensure that both partitions represent the class mix. It does not itself solve dependence between rows or eliminate data leakage.
questions.answerText: Approximately preserve the original class proportions in each split.

questions.prompt: Two classifiers have the same mean cross-validation macro-F1, but one has much higher fold-to-fold standard deviation. What does the higher standard deviation directly indicate?

choices.text: Its observed performance varies more across the validation folds.
Its population mean performance is known exactly.
Its probability predictions are perfectly calibrated.
It necessarily has fewer model parameters.

questions.explanation: Fold standard deviation summarizes the spread of the observed fold scores. It should be considered with the mean, split design, and other practical criteria.
questions.answerText: Its observed performance varies more across the validation folds.

questions.prompt: Why evaluate a DummyClassifier before celebrating a trained classifier's 94% accuracy?

choices.text: A dummy model replaces the need for a test set.
A dummy model proves that the features contain no useful information.
A trivial prediction strategy may already achieve a similar score because of the class distribution.
The trained model must always be less accurate than the dummy.

questions.explanation: A baseline reveals how much performance can be achieved without learning a useful feature relationship. A high headline accuracy may provide little improvement over always predicting the majority class.
questions.answerText: A trivial prediction strategy may already achieve a similar score because of the class distribution.

questions.prompt: A binary classifier has positive-class recall 0.90 and negative-class recall 0.60. What is its balanced accuracy?
questions.explanation: Balanced accuracy is the arithmetic mean of the recalls across classes. Here, (0.90 + 0.60) / 2 = 0.75.

questions.prompt: Which task is an unsupervised analysis?

choices.text: Tune a classifier to maximize validation macro-F1.
Group unlabeled sensor profiles by similarity without fitting to a failure label.
Predict next month's measured energy demand from historical labeled examples.
Predict a known defect label from labeled images.

questions.explanation: Clustering discovers structure without using a target label during fitting. The resulting groups require interpretation and are not automatically the true categories of interest.
questions.answerText: Group unlabeled sensor profiles by similarity without fitting to a failure label.

questions.prompt: For a fitted binary classifier, what does predict_proba(X) generally return?

choices.text: Estimated class probabilities for each row, with columns ordered according to classes_.
The training accuracy repeated for every input row.
A proof that each predicted probability equals the true event frequency.
One cluster identifier per input row.

questions.explanation: The output supplies a probability estimate for each class for each observation. Inspect classes_ before selecting a positive-class column, and assess calibration separately when it matters.
questions.answerText: Estimated class probabilities for each row, with columns ordered according to classes_.

questions.prompt: Why place a nonlinear activation between dense layers?

choices.text: It guarantees zero training error on every possible dataset.
It allows the network to represent relationships that a composition of affine layers alone cannot represent.
It removes the need to learn weights.
It makes every output a calibrated probability.

questions.explanation: Composing affine transformations without intervening nonlinearities yields another affine transformation. Nonlinear activations let depth contribute more expressive relationships.
questions.answerText: It allows the network to represent relationships that a composition of affine layers alone cannot represent.

questions.prompt: A 32 by 32 image enters a convolution with a 3 by 3 kernel, stride 2, dilation 1, and no padding. What is the output spatial size?
questions.explanation: For each axis, the output size is floor((32 - 3) / 2) + 1 = 15. The same calculation applies to height and width under the stated assumptions.

questions.prompt: Why can freezing early layers of a pretrained image CNN be useful for a small new image dataset?

choices.text: The early layers already contain the exact labels of every new task.
Their edge and texture features may transfer while fewer parameters need to be trained.
Frozen layers automatically learn faster than unfrozen layers.
Freezing forces every new image to receive the same prediction.

questions.explanation: Early visual features often capture patterns useful across related image tasks. Freezing these weights reduces the number of trainable parameters, although task suitability still needs validation.
questions.answerText: Their edge and texture features may transfer while fewer parameters need to be trained.

questions.prompt: One channel of a feature map contains [[2, 4], [6, 8]]. What value does Global Average Pooling produce for this channel?
questions.explanation: Global Average Pooling averages all spatial positions within each channel. The channel's average is (2 + 4 + 6 + 8) / 4 = 5.

questions.prompt: A sensor network has many missing humidity readings at high-altitude sites but few at coastal sites. Dropping incomplete rows removes most high-altitude observations. Which revision is most defensible?

choices.text: Drop the high-altitude subgroup so the remaining data look cleaner.
Use test-set humidity values to reconstruct the missing training readings.
Replace all missing readings with the final failure label.
Investigate the missingness and evaluate training-fitted subgroup-aware imputation with a fallback.

questions.explanation: Complete-case deletion can change subgroup representation and undermine the intended deployment population. Investigating missingness and validating a training-fitted imputation policy addresses that risk without using held-out information.
questions.answerText: Investigate the missingness and evaluate training-fitted subgroup-aware imputation with a fallback.

questions.prompt: You want to predict failures on previously unseen sensors. Each sensor contributes many similar daily rows, and a random row split places the same sensors in training and test. What change best matches the intended generalization?

choices.text: Fit the scaler on all sensors before making the same row split.
Hold out entire sensors and fit preprocessing only on the training sensors.
Keep the row split and add sensor ID as a one-hot feature to guarantee generalization.
Evaluate on the training rows because their sensor IDs are known.

questions.explanation: Holding out sensor groups tests transfer to sensors that were not represented during fitting. Overlapping sensor identities can make a row-level test look easier than the actual deployment problem.
questions.answerText: Hold out entire sensors and fit preprocessing only on the training sensors.

questions.prompt: Missing a defective item costs 20 times as much as inspecting a good item. The current classifier flags items when the defect probability is at least 0.50. What is the best next step before deployment?

choices.text: Choose the threshold giving the highest final test accuracy.
Raise the threshold automatically because false negatives are expensive.
Keep 0.50 because every probability classifier requires that threshold.
Use validation data to compare thresholds by the stated error costs, then freeze the choice before final testing.

questions.explanation: Threshold selection should reflect the relative consequences of false negatives and false positives. Validation-based cost comparison supports an explicit operating decision while preserving the final test for evaluation.
questions.answerText: Use validation data to compare thresholds by the stated error costs, then freeze the choice before final testing.

questions.prompt: A deployed pipeline expects temperature_c as a numeric Celsius field. A client sends a string field named temperature_f containing Fahrenheit values. What should happen before prediction?

choices.text: Refit the model on this single unlabeled request.
Ignore field names and pass the string to the model in the same position.
Replace every input field with the predicted class.
Reject or explicitly convert the input using a validated schema and unit-conversion rule.

questions.explanation: Names, data types, and units are part of the model's input contract. Validation should catch the mismatch or apply a documented conversion before the fitted pipeline receives the data.
questions.answerText: Reject or explicitly convert the input using a validated schema and unit-conversion rule.

questions.prompt: A defect detector must retain features near an image's border. A stride-1 convolution with valid padding shrinks its feature map. Which change preserves spatial dimensions for an odd-sized kernel?

choices.text: Use same zero-padding with stride 1.
Remove every border pixel before convolution.
Increase the stride while retaining valid padding.
Apply Global Average Pooling before examining the border.

questions.explanation: Same padding adds border values so a stride-1 convolution can preserve height and width. This permits filter placement at edge locations, although padded values do not add real image information.

questions.prompt: Which practices help prevent preprocessing or selection leakage? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Fit a feature scaler on the full dataset before cross-validation.
Learn missing-value imputation statistics from the training partition.
Place fitted preprocessing inside the cross-validation pipeline.
Choose the final model by repeatedly checking hold-out scores.
Keep the final hold-out untouched while selecting model settings.

questions.explanation: Each validation or test partition must be excluded from the fitted decisions it is used to assess. Training-only imputation, fold-local preprocessing, and an untouched final hold-out support that separation.
questions.answerText: Learn missing-value imputation statistics from the training partition.; Place fitted preprocessing inside the cross-validation pipeline.; Keep the final hold-out untouched while selecting model settings.

questions.prompt: Which statements about evaluating a rare positive class are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A ROC curve becomes mathematically invalid whenever class counts differ.
A precision-recall curve can be especially informative about positive-class retrieval under imbalance.
Macro-F1 averages class-specific F1 scores without weighting by class frequency.
High accuracy alone establishes that the rare positive class is detected well.
Balanced accuracy gives each class's recall equal weight.

questions.explanation: Balanced accuracy and macro-F1 expose class-level performance that overall accuracy can hide. Precision-recall analysis is often useful under imbalance, while ROC analysis remains valid and answers a different rate-based question.
questions.answerText: A precision-recall curve can be especially informative about positive-class retrieval under imbalance.; Macro-F1 averages class-specific F1 scores without weighting by class frequency.; Balanced accuracy gives each class's recall equal weight.

questions.prompt: Which should accompany a deployable tabular classification artifact? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A fresh unfitted encoder that discovers a new feature order on every request.
Reference inputs with expected outputs for a prediction sanity test.
The fitted imputer, encoder, scaler, and classifier required by its workflow.
Only a screenshot of the best validation score.
The expected input schema, including feature meanings and units.

questions.explanation: Reproducing predictions requires the fitted transformations as well as the estimator. Schema information and reference predictions help detect incompatible inputs or changes in the serving workflow.
questions.answerText: Reference inputs with expected outputs for a prediction sanity test.; The fitted imputer, encoder, scaler, and classifier required by its workflow.; The expected input schema, including feature meanings and units.

questions.prompt: Which conclusions about a K-Means result are justified? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The K with the lowest training inertia is automatically the best substantive choice regardless of size.
The cluster identifiers are arbitrary group labels that need interpretation.
Silhouette scores can contribute evidence about cohesion and separation.
A clean-looking 2D PCA plot proves that all original-space clusters are well separated.
Cluster 0 is necessarily the healthy class and cluster 1 the faulty class.

questions.explanation: K-Means produces geometric groups whose meanings are not supplied by the algorithm. Diagnostics such as silhouette and an elbow should be considered with domain knowledge and the limitations of visual projections.
questions.answerText: The cluster identifiers are arbitrary group labels that need interpretation.; Silhouette scores can contribute evidence about cohesion and separation.

questions.prompt: A sensor classifier is live, but verified outcome labels arrive a month later. Which monitoring actions or interpretations are justified now? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Conclude that accuracy has definitely fallen whenever an input histogram changes.
Investigate flagged shifts and document whether a sensor, collection process, or operating condition changed.
Compare current feature distributions with the documented training or deployment reference.
Track missing-value rates and feature variance to detect changes in incoming data.
Automatically retrain on the model's unverified predictions whenever an alert appears.

questions.explanation: Feature distributions, missingness, and variance provide observable signals before verified labels arrive. Alerts call for investigation and do not by themselves prove degraded accuracy or justify automatic retraining.
questions.answerText: Investigate flagged shifts and document whether a sensor, collection process, or operating condition changed.; Compare current feature distributions with the documented training or deployment reference.; Track missing-value rates and feature variance to detect changes in incoming data.

questions.prompt: A standard MaxPooling operation learns a separate weight for every value in its pooling window.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: MaxPooling selects the largest value in each specified window. The standard operation has no learned filter weights.

questions.prompt: When a complete preprocessing-and-classifier Pipeline is passed to cross-validation, each fold can fit its transformations using only that fold's training subset.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Cross-validation fits a separate estimator workflow for each training fold. Keeping fitted transformations inside that workflow prevents the held-out fold from contributing their learned statistics.

questions.prompt: A two-dimensional PCA plot preserves every distance and every separation present in a high-dimensional feature space.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A 2D projection generally discards information from the remaining dimensions. It is a visual aid rather than proof of the full geometry or of valid class labels.

questions.prompt: Preserving class proportions with a stratified split is sufficient to prevent leakage from repeated observations of the same individual.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Stratification controls class proportions rather than the identities or dependencies shared across partitions. A split must also respect groups or time when the intended deployment requires that separation.

questions.prompt: In an allowed AI-assisted notebook, a useful verification log records which suggestions were accepted, corrected, or rejected, along with the evidence and the final human decision.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A verification log makes the human review of AI suggestions traceable. Recording corrections, rejections, evidence, and the final decision is more informative than merely naming the tool.

questions.prompt: An inertia elbow can suggest a point of diminishing improvement as K grows, but it should be considered with other evidence when choosing K.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Adding clusters generally reduces the best achievable training inertia, so a decrease alone does not identify the most useful grouping. An elbow is a heuristic that benefits from silhouette evidence and domain interpretation.

questions.prompt: For a stride-1 convolution, same padding can preserve the input's height and width.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Same padding adds enough border values to maintain spatial dimensions at stride 1. The number of output channels is still determined by the convolution's filters.

questions.prompt: Several dense layers with only affine transformations and no nonlinear activation between them can be represented by a single affine transformation.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Composing matrix multiplications and biases produces another matrix multiplication and bias. Depth alone therefore does not provide a nonlinear decision relationship.

questions.prompt: Recording a dataset's source, collection period, and transformation history helps another person audit how the modeling data were produced.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Provenance records trace the path from source data to modeling inputs. This supports reproducibility and investigation of unexpected values or results.

questions.prompt: Freezing a pretrained convolutional layer means its kernel weights are updated automatically during each training step on the new task.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Frozen kernel weights are excluded from the new task's trainable weight updates. Later fine-tuning can explicitly unfreeze selected layers if justified.

questions.prompt: A precision-recall curve helps examine the tradeoff between finding positive cases and the fraction of flagged cases that are actually positive as a threshold changes.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Recall measures the fraction of actual positives that are found, while precision measures the fraction of flagged cases that are positive. Varying the threshold traces the tradeoff between these quantities.

questions.prompt: For a finite real-valued input, the sigmoid activation produces a value strictly between 0 and 1.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Sigmoid is defined as 1 / (1 + exp(-x)). Its mathematical output lies between zero and one, approaching the endpoints as the input becomes extreme.

questions.prompt: A StandardScaler fitted on training data guarantees that every future test batch will have exactly zero mean and unit variance after transformation.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The transformation uses the training mean and scale. A test batch can have a different distribution, so its transformed mean and variance need not equal zero and one.

questions.prompt: If K-Means assigns an observation to cluster 2, the number 2 itself represents a measured severity level.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Cluster numbers identify groups and carry no inherent order or severity meaning. A severity interpretation requires separate evidence from the application domain.

questions.prompt: On a dataset with 99% negative cases, a classifier that always predicts negative has 99% accuracy and therefore must be a useful detector of positive cases.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The classifier never identifies a positive case, so its positive recall is zero. Overall accuracy can be dominated by the majority class and does not establish useful positive detection.

questions.prompt: Fill in the exact scikit-learn class name: from sklearn.preprocessing import ____ . This class learns means and scales for standardization.
questions.explanation: StandardScaler learns feature means and scales during fit. Reuse that fitted transformation for validation and test data.

questions.prompt: The encoding method that represents a category using separate indicator columns, rather than an artificial numerical ranking, is called ____ encoding.
questions.explanation: One-hot encoding uses category-specific indicator features. The fitted category-to-column mapping must remain aligned at inference.

questions.prompt: A Pipeline names its classifier step model. Fill in the exact GridSearchCV parameter key used to tune that classifier's C parameter: ____ .
questions.explanation: Pipeline parameters use the step name, two underscores, and the estimator parameter name. The correct key is model__C, with an uppercase C.

questions.prompt: Three points have Euclidean distances 1, 2, and 3 from their assigned centroids. Using the sum of squared distances definition, the total inertia is ____ .
questions.explanation: Inertia sums squared distances to the assigned centroids. The calculation is 1 squared + 2 squared + 3 squared = 14.

questions.prompt: Higher cross-validation scores are better. The best model's mean score is 0.86 and its estimated standard error is 0.02. Under the One-Standard-Error rule, the minimum eligible mean score is ____ .
questions.explanation: For a score to maximize, the eligibility boundary is the best mean minus one standard error. This gives 0.86 - 0.02 = 0.84, after which the simplest eligible candidate is preferred.

questions.prompt: After import joblib, fill in the exact qualified function name used to save a fitted full pipeline: ____(pipeline, 'model.joblib').
questions.explanation: joblib.dump serializes the supplied fitted object. Saving the complete pipeline preserves its learned preprocessing together with its classifier.

questions.prompt: A square input has width 30. A convolution uses kernel width 5, stride 1, dilation 1, and valid padding. Its output width is ____ .
questions.explanation: With no padding and stride 1, the output width is input width minus kernel width plus one. Here, 30 - 5 + 1 = 26.

questions.prompt: The standard activation defined by f(x) = max(0, x) is ____ .
questions.explanation: ReLU keeps positive inputs and maps negative inputs to zero. Its nonlinear form helps a network avoid affine-layer collapse.

questions.prompt: Ignoring the batch dimension, a feature tensor has shape 4 by 4 by 128, with 128 channels. Global Average Pooling over the two spatial axes produces ____ output values.
questions.explanation: Global Average Pooling averages spatial positions separately within each channel. It therefore returns one value per channel, or 128 values here.

questions.prompt: Using sigmoid(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(-x)), sigmoid(0) equals ____ .
questions.explanation: At x = 0, exp(-x) equals 1. The output is therefore 1 / (1 + 1) = 0.5.

questions.prompt: Which finding most strongly challenges a plan to drop every row with a missing feature?

choices.text: The missing rows include numeric and categorical fields.
The dataset can be opened in more than one software application.
The missing rows use the same column names as the complete rows.
Missingness is concentrated in a subgroup that the deployed model must serve.

questions.explanation: Dropping rows selectively can change the population represented in training and evaluation. The missingness mechanism and subgroup coverage should inform the preprocessing policy.
questions.answerText: Missingness is concentrated in a subgroup that the deployed model must serve.

questions.prompt: A fitted one-hot encoder encounters a new category in a live request. What is the soundest design principle?

choices.text: Shift every existing feature one position to make room for the new category.
Define and validate an explicit unknown-category policy while retaining the fitted feature schema.
Create a new input column and silently append it to the model's expected vector.
Map the new category to the target class with the same name.

questions.explanation: Unseen categories need a deliberate policy, such as validated rejection or a configured unknown handling rule. Arbitrarily changing the encoded columns breaks the feature representation the model learned.
questions.answerText: Define and validate an explicit unknown-category policy while retaining the fitted feature schema.

questions.prompt: A training-fitted scaler has mean 50 and scale 10 for one feature. What transformed value should it assign to a live observation with value 70?
questions.explanation: Standardization subtracts the fitted mean and divides by the fitted scale. The result is (70 - 50) / 10 = 2.

questions.prompt: A team cannot explain why its cleaned dataset differs from last week's version. Which record would most directly help trace the difference?

choices.text: Only the number of layers in the classifier.
A new model trained without retaining any earlier outputs.
The color theme used in the team's report.
Versioned raw-data identifiers and a recorded sequence of cleaning transformations.

questions.explanation: Versioned sources and transformation history make changes traceable. This provenance helps distinguish an intentional cleaning revision from an accidental data change.
questions.answerText: Versioned raw-data identifiers and a recorded sequence of cleaning transformations.

questions.prompt: Live sensor values shift toward a hotter operating range, while the conditional relationship P(failure | sensor values) is assumed unchanged. Which description best fits the stated change?

choices.text: Covariate drift in the input distribution.
Proof that the model's labels have been permuted.
Concept drift defined specifically as a changed conditional relationship.
Proof that the input schema is invalid.

questions.explanation: Covariate drift refers to a change in the distribution of inputs. Under the stated assumption, the feature-to-outcome relationship has not changed, so that evidence alone does not establish concept drift.
questions.answerText: Covariate drift in the input distribution.

questions.prompt: A report presents only the highest score observed in any one validation fold for each model. Which revision gives a more defensible comparison?

choices.text: Choose the model whose best fold happens to contain the fewest positive cases.
Remove every fold in which the preferred model underperforms.
Replace validation results with training scores only.
Report the mean and variability across the same folds, alongside relevant runtime and baseline comparisons.

questions.explanation: A single favorable fold can give a misleading picture of generalization. Mean performance, variability, practical constraints, and baseline improvement support a broader comparison.
questions.answerText: Report the mean and variability across the same folds, alongside relevant runtime and baseline comparisons.

questions.prompt: A team has trained a classifier and must select a decision threshold before reporting a final performance estimate. Which order preserves the final hold-out's role?

choices.text: Refit preprocessing on the hold-out and then select its best threshold.
Choose the threshold that makes the training accuracy exactly 100%.
Select the threshold using validation predictions, lock it, and evaluate once on the final hold-out.
Choose the threshold using hold-out labels, then report the same hold-out score as an independent estimate.

questions.explanation: Threshold selection is a fitted decision and needs its own development data. Freezing it before final testing protects the hold-out from selection bias.
questions.answerText: Select the threshold using validation predictions, lock it, and evaluate once on the final hold-out.

questions.prompt: A two-class model has class-specific F1 scores of 0.80 and 0.40. What is macro-F1?
questions.explanation: Macro-F1 is the unweighted arithmetic mean of the class-specific F1 scores. Here, (0.80 + 0.40) / 2 = 0.60.

questions.prompt: A detector flags 15 items, of which 12 are truly defective and 3 are good. What is precision for the defective class?

choices.text: It cannot be calculated without the number of true negatives.

questions.explanation: Precision is TP / (TP + FP), the fraction of positive predictions that are correct. The calculation is 12 / (12 + 3) = 0.80 and does not require true negatives.

questions.prompt: K-Means inertia decreases as K increases from 2 to 20. Why is choosing K = 20 solely because it has the smallest inertia inadequate?

choices.text: More clusters can fit the training geometry better without yielding the most useful or interpretable grouping.
Inertia must increase whenever another centroid is added.
K-Means automatically knows the true number of classes from the target label.
Inertia is only defined when K equals 2.

questions.explanation: The best achievable inertia generally falls as more centroids are available. Choosing K also needs evidence about separation, stability, interpretability, and the task's purpose.
questions.answerText: More clusters can fit the training geometry better without yielding the most useful or interpretable grouping.

questions.prompt: What does a two-component PCA projection primarily try to preserve when used as a visualization of standardized features?

choices.text: Every original pairwise distance exactly.
As much variance as possible within a two-dimensional linear projection.
The semantic meaning of the first two original columns only.
The class labels and their classification accuracy.

questions.explanation: PCA chooses orthogonal directions that retain variance in the projected data. High retained variance does not by itself prove class separation or validate a clustering interpretation.
questions.answerText: As much variance as possible within a two-dimensional linear projection.

questions.prompt: A binary neural network has a sigmoid output of 0.90 for an image. Which interpretation is most careful?

choices.text: The model's classification threshold must therefore be 0.90.
The image contains exactly 90 positive pixels.
The network is guaranteed to be correct on exactly 90% of all future images.
This is an estimated positive-class probability, whose calibration and predictive performance need separate evaluation.

questions.explanation: A sigmoid output can serve as a binary probability estimate in the appropriate classification setup. Being bounded between zero and one does not guarantee that the estimates are calibrated.
questions.answerText: This is an estimated positive-class probability, whose calibration and predictive performance need separate evaluation.

questions.prompt: What does weight sharing mean in a convolutional layer?

choices.text: A learned filter uses the same kernel weights as it moves across spatial positions.
Each spatial location learns a completely independent kernel for the same filter.
Every layer in the network must use an identical weight matrix.
Every image in the dataset must have the same pixel intensities.

questions.explanation: A convolution reuses each filter's weights across the input's spatial positions. This reduces parameter requirements and lets the same local pattern be detected in different locations.
questions.answerText: A learned filter uses the same kernel weights as it moves across spatial positions.

questions.prompt: A 24 by 24 feature map passes through 2 by 2 MaxPooling with stride 2 and no padding. What is its output spatial size?
questions.explanation: Each nonoverlapping 2 by 2 window produces one value. With an even input size of 24, both spatial dimensions are reduced to 12.

questions.prompt: A pretrained CNN backbone is frozen and a new classifier head is added. Which weights are intended to learn during this initial transfer-learning stage?

choices.text: Every input pixel, treated as a trainable model parameter.
Only the frozen convolution kernels.
The trainable weights of the new classifier head.
No weights anywhere, so predictions cannot change.

questions.explanation: Freezing the backbone leaves its kernel weights unchanged during this stage. The new trainable head learns to map the retained representation to the new task's outputs.
questions.answerText: The trainable weights of the new classifier head.

questions.prompt: A training-fitted imputer uses a median for each factory. A new factory appears in deployment with a missing measurement, and it has no training-fitted median. Which response best preserves the fitted workflow?

choices.text: Apply a documented fallback, such as a global median fitted on training data, and record the unseen group.
Compute its median from the hidden target labels.
Set the missing feature equal to the factory's text name.
Use the final test-set mean without recording the change.

questions.explanation: A subgroup-aware imputer needs a defined policy for groups without fitted statistics. A training-fitted fallback keeps inference reproducible while logging highlights a potentially important change in deployment coverage.
questions.answerText: Apply a documented fallback, such as a global median fitted on training data, and record the unseen group.

questions.prompt: At noon, a sensor model predicts whether a breakdown will occur before midnight. A proposed feature is the day's maximum vibration calculated from readings through midnight. Which revision is necessary?

choices.text: Include the actual breakdown result as another input to balance the feature.
Normalize the feature using all future days to remove leakage.
Define the feature using readings available by noon only, then evaluate the revised workflow.
Keep the feature because all readings occur on the same calendar day.

questions.explanation: The full-day maximum uses readings unavailable at the noon prediction moment. Restricting the feature window to available information makes the evaluation match the deployed task.
questions.answerText: Define the feature using readings available by noon only, then evaluate the revised workflow.

questions.prompt: On four validation items, defect probabilities and labels are (0.9, defect), (0.6, good), (0.4, defect), and (0.1, good). Flag an item when p is at least the threshold. With false-negative cost 10 and false-positive cost 1, which option has lower total cost?

choices.text: Threshold 0.5, with total cost 0.
Threshold 0.3, with total cost 11.
Threshold 0.5, with total cost 1.
Threshold 0.3, with total cost 1.

questions.explanation: At threshold 0.3, both defects are found and only the 0.6 good item is falsely flagged, costing 1. At threshold 0.5, there is one false positive and one missed defect, costing 1 + 10 = 11.

questions.prompt: After moving a model to a server, the same saved reference input gives a very different probability from the verified notebook result. What should the team investigate first?

choices.text: Whether artifact versions, preprocessing, feature schema, and inference settings match the verified workflow.
Whether the new probability can be reported without checking the workflow.
Whether adding more screenshots will increase the probability.
Whether the reference label can be changed to match the new prediction.

questions.explanation: A reference input provides a controlled check of the serving path. A mismatch points to a need to inspect the artifact and input-processing contract before trusting live predictions.
questions.answerText: Whether artifact versions, preprocessing, feature schema, and inference settings match the verified workflow.

questions.prompt: A border-sensitive image model uses a 5 by 5 convolution with stride 1 and dilation 1. How many zero-padding pixels must be added on each side to keep height and width unchanged?
questions.explanation: The stride-1 size equation is output = input + 2P - 5 + 1. Setting output equal to input gives 2P = 4, so P = 2 on each side.

questions.prompt: A team is reviewing a tabular preprocessing plan. Which choices are sound? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Estimate subgroup imputation medians separately within each cross-validation training fold.
Choose which features to retain by repeatedly examining final test labels.
Exclude features that would only become available after the prediction moment.
Learn one-hot category mappings from all rows before creating the hold-out.
Use the fitted training transformations unchanged when evaluating the held-out partition.

questions.explanation: Fitted preprocessing must exclude the observations it is used to evaluate, and input availability must match deployment. Fold-local fitting, reused training transformations, and prediction-time feature checks support those requirements.
questions.answerText: Estimate subgroup imputation medians separately within each cross-validation training fold.; Exclude features that would only become available after the prediction moment.; Use the fitted training transformations unchanged when evaluating the held-out partition.

questions.prompt: A rare-event classifier has excellent overall accuracy but low minority-class recall. Which evaluation choices would provide useful additional evidence? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Conclude that the detector works well solely because accuracy is high.
Inspect the confusion matrix and class-specific recall.
Remove missed positive cases from the evaluation set.
Inspect precision-recall behavior across candidate thresholds.
Report macro-F1 or balanced accuracy alongside the baseline.

questions.explanation: These checks expose how the classifier handles the rare class and the tradeoff among operating points. A baseline and class-aware metrics make a high accuracy figure easier to interpret.
questions.answerText: Inspect the confusion matrix and class-specific recall.; Inspect precision-recall behavior across candidate thresholds.; Report macro-F1 or balanced accuracy alongside the baseline.

questions.prompt: Which practices support reproducible predictions after exporting a fitted model? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Check loaded predictions against saved reference inputs and outputs.
Save and load the full fitted preprocessing-plus-model pipeline.
Record relevant dependency versions and the expected feature schema.
Refit the scaler independently on each individual prediction request.
Export only classifier coefficients and discard the fitted encoder's category order.

questions.explanation: A model depends on its learned preprocessing and a compatible serving environment. Version records, a stable schema, and reference checks help identify changes that would alter predictions.
questions.answerText: Check loaded predictions against saved reference inputs and outputs.; Save and load the full fitted preprocessing-plus-model pipeline.; Record relevant dependency versions and the expected feature schema.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe a defensible unsupervised clustering workflow? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Assume cluster identifiers must match the numerical coding of known classes.
Exclude the outcome label from the features used to fit an unsupervised grouping.
Use external labels, if available, as separate interpretation or evaluation evidence rather than as hidden fitting inputs.
Consider scaling because K-Means uses Euclidean geometry.
Declare the grouping valid solely because two colors separate in one PCA view.

questions.explanation: An unsupervised fit should not secretly incorporate the outcome it is later compared with. Scaling and separate interpretation checks help assess what the geometric groups actually represent.
questions.answerText: Exclude the outcome label from the features used to fit an unsupervised grouping.; Use external labels, if available, as separate interpretation or evaluation evidence rather than as hidden fitting inputs.; Consider scaling because K-Means uses Euclidean geometry.

questions.prompt: A team monitors a deployed vision model and its incoming data. Which practices are appropriate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Where verified labels become available, assess current predictive performance as well as input changes.
Silently retrain on unverified machine predictions whenever an alert appears.
Treat every input-distribution alert as proof that the conditional feature-to-label relationship has changed.
Investigate alerts and document the evidence behind a human decision to revise or retain the model.
Track input distributions and missingness against a documented reference.

questions.explanation: Input monitoring and labeled performance checks supply different kinds of evidence. Documented human review helps turn those signals into accountable operational decisions.
questions.answerText: Where verified labels become available, assess current predictive performance as well as input changes.; Investigate alerts and document the evidence behind a human decision to revise or retain the model.; Track input distributions and missingness against a documented reference.

questions.prompt: Global Average Pooling over height and width always merges all feature channels into a single scalar.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The spatial average is computed separately for each channel. A tensor with C channels therefore produces C values when the spatial axes are pooled.

questions.prompt: A convolutional filter can detect a similar local pattern at several image positions using the same learned kernel weights.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The filter is applied across spatial positions rather than learning a new kernel at each location. This weight sharing is a central property of convolution.

questions.prompt: Loading a saved fitted preprocessing-plus-model pipeline helps apply the same learned transformations used during development to new inputs.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The saved workflow retains fitted transformation parameters and the estimator together. Input-schema checks are still needed to confirm that new data satisfy its expectations.

questions.prompt: After features have been standardized, the decision threshold is automatically calibrated to the business costs of false positives and false negatives.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Feature standardization changes numerical inputs rather than selecting an operating decision rule. Threshold selection and probability calibration are separate procedures that require appropriate validation.

questions.prompt: Even if two one-hot encoded arrays have the same width, changing which category occupies each column can invalidate the model's interpretation of an input.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Input positions have learned meanings, not just a required count. A schema mismatch can silently associate a value with the wrong learned feature.

questions.prompt: A frozen pretrained backbone guarantees perfect accuracy on any new image domain, so validation is unnecessary.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Transfer depends on how well the learned representation suits the new task and data. Validation is needed to assess whether freezing or fine-tuning is appropriate.

questions.prompt: When K-Means is run with K equal to the number of known classes, its clusters necessarily reproduce those class labels.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: K-Means optimizes distance to centroids rather than agreement with hidden class meanings. Equal counts of clusters and classes do not guarantee matching memberships.

questions.prompt: Reporting cross-validation mean and standard deviation is more informative about observed performance consistency than reporting the mean alone.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The mean summarizes average observed performance while the standard deviation describes spread across folds. Neither removes the need for an appropriate split design and a final evaluation.

questions.prompt: Trying many model settings against the same final hold-out and keeping the best one leaves that hold-out fully independent of model selection.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Repeated comparison makes the hold-out part of the selection process. Its reported best score can then be optimistic, so model selection belongs in training and validation workflows.

questions.prompt: ROC analysis must always be discarded as mathematically invalid whenever the positive class is rare.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: ROC analysis remains defined under class imbalance when both classes are present. Precision-recall analysis often provides especially relevant positive-class information, but that does not make ROC universally invalid.

questions.prompt: Standard ReLU preserves a negative input unchanged so the network remains nonlinear.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Standard ReLU outputs zero for negative inputs and keeps positive inputs. This piecewise behavior is the source of its nonlinearity.

questions.prompt: An AI-generated neural-network notebook can run without errors and still require independent checks of tensor shapes, metric calculations, and whether its interpretation matches the actual outputs.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Successful execution confirms that code ran, not that its shapes, measurements, or conclusions are correct. Independent checks against the intended architecture and observed results can reveal semantic mistakes that execution alone misses.

questions.topic: Balanced accuracy of a constant classifier
questions.prompt: In a binary test set containing both classes, a classifier that predicts every case as positive has balanced accuracy 0.50.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Positive-class recall is 1 and negative-class recall is 0. Their mean is (1 + 0) / 2 = 0.50 regardless of the class proportions.

questions.prompt: Disclosing the use of an AI assistant does not remove the human author's responsibility to verify the final analysis and follow assessment rules.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Disclosure explains how assistance was used, while verification addresses whether the work is sound. The human author remains responsible for the final choices and for complying with the specific assessment's restrictions.

questions.prompt: It is safe to fit an imputer on the entire dataset before a train-test split because imputation does not use class labels.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Fitted imputation still learns from the held-out feature distribution. Training-only fitting is required even when a transformation does not use the target.

questions.prompt: A structured reference listing each dataset field's meaning, type, units, and allowed values is called a data ____ .
questions.explanation: A data dictionary documents the meaning and constraints of individual fields. It helps users interpret measurements and validate incoming values consistently.

questions.prompt: Within one training subgroup, the nonmissing values are 1, 2, and 100. A subgroup-median imputer fills a missing value in that group with ____ .
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value after ordering the observed training values. For 1, 2, and 100, that value is 2 rather than the much larger mean.

questions.prompt: Among 20 truly defective items, a detector finds 16 and misses 4. Its defect-class recall is ____ as a decimal.
questions.explanation: Recall is TP / (TP + FN). The calculation is 16 / (16 + 4) = 0.8.

questions.prompt: A fitted scikit-learn classifier supports probability estimates. Fill in the exact method name: model.____(X_new).
questions.explanation: predict_proba returns class probability estimates rather than only the chosen class labels. Check the estimator's classes_ ordering before selecting a positive-class probability column.

questions.prompt: A K-Means cluster contains only the two points (2, 4) and (4, 8). Its centroid is ____; enter an ordered pair.
questions.explanation: A K-Means centroid is the coordinate-wise mean of the assigned points. Averaging the coordinates gives ((2 + 4) / 2, (4 + 8) / 2) = (3, 6).

questions.prompt: For this exercise, estimate standard error as fold-score SD divided by sqrt(k). The best mean validation score is 0.90, fold-score SD is 0.04, and k = 4. For a score to maximize, the One-Standard-Error eligibility boundary is ____ .
questions.explanation: Using the specified estimate, SE = 0.04 / sqrt(4) = 0.02. The boundary is 0.90 - 0.02 = 0.88, so using the fold standard deviation directly would give the wrong result.

questions.prompt: A 32 by 32 input enters a 5 by 5 convolution with stride 1, dilation 1, and no padding. The output height is ____ .
questions.explanation: Valid padding adds no border values, so the kernel must fit entirely within the input. The height is 32 - 5 + 1 = 28.

questions.prompt: A single 2 by 2 MaxPooling window contains [[1, 5], [3, 2]]. The pooled output value is ____ .
questions.explanation: MaxPooling selects the largest activation in the pooling window. The largest value among 1, 5, 3, and 2 is 5.

questions.prompt: The spatial pooling operation that replaces each entire feature-map channel with its mean is called ____; use the full operation name.
questions.explanation: Global Average Pooling produces one spatial mean per channel. Compared with flattening a large feature map, it can greatly reduce the size and parameter count of a following dense head.

questions.prompt: Using standard ReLU(x) = max(0, x), ReLU(-7) equals ____ .
questions.explanation: Standard ReLU clips negative inputs to zero. Since -7 is negative, the output is 0.

questions.prompt: Two equipment models have very different normal operating temperatures. Each has enough observed training values. Which imputation is most defensible for missing temperatures?

choices.text: Use the median from the corresponding equipment model, estimated on training data.
Delete every record from the model with more missing values.
Use a single median computed from training and test records together.
Replace missing values with the largest temperature observed in either model.

questions.explanation: Subgroup estimates can preserve meaningful operating differences that a global value would blur. Estimate them from training data and define a fallback for subgroups without enough observations.
questions.answerText: Use the median from the corresponding equipment model, estimated on training data.

questions.prompt: A KNN model uses distance in kilometers and vibration in millimeters. Why consider StandardScaler before calculating distances?

choices.text: It converts KNN into a probabilistic generative model.
It guarantees equal predictive importance for every feature.
It removes the need to choose the number of neighbors.
It reduces domination by features with larger numeric scales.

questions.explanation: Standardization centers each nonconstant training feature and scales it by its training standard deviation. This changes distance geometry but does not guarantee equal relevance or eliminate model selection.
questions.answerText: It reduces domination by features with larger numeric scales.

questions.prompt: A training encoder produces columns [color_blue, color_red]. Why must inference use that fitted encoder rather than independently encoding each incoming batch?

choices.text: The model expects consistent column meanings and ordering.
Incoming batches must contain the same number of rows as training.
One-hot encoding learns the correct target for each color.
Independent encoding necessarily creates duplicate observations.

questions.explanation: A feature position has a specific learned meaning. Independent encoding can omit absent categories or reorder columns, making otherwise plausible numeric inputs mean something different to the model.
questions.answerText: The model expects consistent column meanings and ordering.

questions.prompt: A table contains a field named temp with no units or collection details. Which addition most directly improves reproducibility and correct interpretation?

choices.text: A higher number of displayed decimal places.
A random row order and a new file name.
A dictionary specifying units, source, collection time, and missing-value codes.
A claim that every recorded value is accurate.

questions.explanation: A data dictionary explains field semantics, while provenance records where the data came from and how it was collected. Those details help detect unit mismatches and reproduce processing decisions.
questions.answerText: A dictionary specifying units, source, collection time, and missing-value codes.

questions.prompt: A three-class classifier has class F1 scores of 0.90, 0.60, and 0.30. What is its macro-F1?

choices.text: Cannot be computed without class frequencies.

questions.explanation: Macro-F1 is the unweighted mean of the per-class F1 scores: (0.90 + 0.60 + 0.30) / 3 = 0.60. Unlike a support-weighted average, it gives each class equal weight.

questions.prompt: A binary model correctly identifies 90 of 100 negatives and 6 of 20 positives. What is balanced accuracy?
questions.explanation: Negative-class recall is 0.90 and positive-class recall is 0.30, so balanced accuracy is their mean, 0.60. Ordinary accuracy would be 96/120 = 0.80 and obscures poor positive-class recall.

questions.prompt: Models A and B have equal mean validation scores. A has noticeably larger fold-to-fold standard deviation. What is the most defensible interpretation?

choices.text: A's performance appears more sensitive to the sampled folds; inspect stability and context.
The equal means make the standard deviations irrelevant.
B has zero risk of failure after deployment.
A is statistically proven to be less accurate on every future dataset.

questions.explanation: Fold standard deviation describes variation across the chosen validation splits. It is useful evidence about stability, but does not by itself establish a universal ranking or a formal confidence guarantee.
questions.answerText: A's performance appears more sensitive to the sampled folds; inspect stability and context.

questions.prompt: Only 1% of examples are positive, and reviewers care about the fraction of alerts that are correct. Which statement best guides curve selection?

choices.text: ROC-AUC is mathematically undefined whenever positives are rare.
Inspect PR behavior for alert quality and recall; ROC can still provide complementary ranking information.
A PR curve removes the need to report prevalence.
A high ROC-AUC guarantees high precision at every threshold.

questions.explanation: Precision directly describes correct alerts among all positive predictions and depends on prevalence. ROC remains valid with both classes present, but its false-positive-rate denominator can make operational alert burden less obvious.
questions.answerText: Inspect PR behavior for alert quality and recall; ROC can still provide complementary ranking information.

questions.prompt: An analyst wants to predict whether a banknote is genuine using examples with verified genuine/forged labels. Which learning setup directly matches that task?

choices.text: PCA with components automatically interpreted as genuine/forged labels.
Unsupervised clustering whose numeric IDs are assumed to be class labels.
Supervised classification using the verified labels as the target.
K-Means with the verified label included as an input feature.

questions.explanation: Verified targets make this a supervised classification problem. Clustering can explore structure, but its cluster IDs do not inherently represent the desired classes.
questions.answerText: Supervised classification using the verified labels as the target.

questions.prompt: Inertia falls as K increases from 2 to 10. Which next step is most appropriate before selecting K?

choices.text: Always choose K=10 because it has the lowest inertia.
Choose the K whose PCA chart has the brightest colors.
Compare elbow behavior, silhouette, cluster sizes, and domain usefulness.
Assign class meanings to cluster IDs in ascending numeric order.

questions.explanation: Inertia generally decreases as more centers are allowed, so the smallest observed value alone does not settle K. Multiple geometric and practical checks help identify a useful partition.
questions.answerText: Compare elbow behavior, silhouette, cluster sizes, and domain usefulness.

questions.prompt: A Pipeline has steps named scale and model, with a classifier exposing parameter C. Which parameter-grid key correctly tunes C?

choices.text: model__C
Pipeline::C
model_C
scale.C

questions.explanation: Pipeline parameter names use the step name, two underscores, and the estimator parameter. The key must match the actual step name, so model__C addresses C in the model step.

questions.prompt: Two scalar dense layers have no activation between them: h(x) = 2x + 1 and y(h) = 3h - 2. What single mapping describes their composition?
questions.explanation: Substitution gives y = 3(2x + 1) - 2 = 6x + 1. The two affine layers still form a single affine map, illustrating why depth needs intervening nonlinear activations to add nonlinear expressiveness.

questions.prompt: A channels-last image is 32 x 32 x 3. A Conv2D layer uses 12 filters, a 5 x 5 kernel, stride 1, dilation 1, and valid padding. What is its output shape, excluding batch?
questions.explanation: Valid padding adds no border, so each spatial dimension is (32 - 5)/1 + 1 = 28. The 12 filters determine the 12 output channels.

questions.prompt: A feature tensor has shape 8 x 8 x 64, excluding batch. With default keepdims=False, what does GlobalAveragePooling2D produce?

choices.text: A vector of 8 values, one per image row.
A vector of 64 values, each averaging one channel's spatial positions.
A vector of 4,096 values.
A single value averaging every channel and position.

questions.explanation: Global Average Pooling reduces the height and width dimensions independently within each channel. It produces 64 channel summaries instead of the 4,096 entries produced by flattening.
questions.answerText: A vector of 64 values, each averaging one channel's spatial positions.

questions.prompt: A pretrained backbone has 1,000,000 parameters and a new head has 2,050 parameters. All backbone parameters are frozen and all head parameters are trainable. How many parameters are eligible for optimizer updates in this stage?
questions.explanation: Only the 2,050 trainable head parameters are eligible for optimizer updates. The frozen backbone still computes representations during the forward pass, while its parameters remain fixed.

questions.prompt: In a maintenance dataset, an older machine family has more missing pressure readings. Dropping every incomplete row removes most of that family. Which response best addresses the problem?

choices.text: Impute using the final failure label, which is unavailable at prediction time.
Inspect subgroup missingness, use justified training-only imputation, and compare retained subgroup representation.
Keep dropping rows until every subgroup has identical sample counts.
Fill from a combined training/test median so the family is represented.

questions.explanation: Complete-case deletion can change which populations remain in the data. A documented subgroup-aware strategy should use only information available at prediction time and be evaluated for both representation and predictive effects.
questions.answerText: Inspect subgroup missingness, use justified training-only imputation, and compare retained subgroup representation.

questions.topic: Sensor network group and time leakage
questions.prompt: A model will predict next month's failures on newly installed sensors. Historical records contain repeated hourly rows per sensor. Which evaluation best matches that deployment?

choices.text: Randomly split hourly rows so each sensor appears in both sets.
Hold out sensor IDs but train on records collected after the validation period.
Use later-period validation records from held-out sensor IDs, with training restricted to earlier data and preprocessing fit only on training.
Split by month but allow the same sensor's adjacent readings in both sets regardless of the new-sensor objective.

questions.explanation: The deployment includes both a future period and unseen sensors, so both time and sensor identity matter. Random row splits or a single constraint can leave an evaluation mismatch and overly optimistic results.
questions.answerText: Use later-period validation records from held-out sensor IDs, with training restricted to earlier data and preprocessing fit only on training.

questions.prompt: On validation data, threshold 0.50 yields 20 missed defects and 5 false alarms; threshold 0.25 yields 8 missed defects and 17 false alarms. Each missed defect costs 10 units and each false alarm 1 unit. Ignoring other costs, which choice is justified?

choices.text: Choose between them using the final test labels, then report that test result.
Choose 0.50 because fewer false alarms always means lower total cost.
Choose 0.25 because lowering thresholds always increases precision.
Choose 0.25 because its estimated cost is 97, versus 205 for 0.50.

questions.explanation: The validation costs are 8 x 10 + 17 = 97 and 20 x 10 + 5 = 205. Select and freeze the operating threshold using validation evidence before the final test.
questions.answerText: Choose 0.25 because its estimated cost is 97, versus 205 for 0.50.

questions.prompt: A deployed model expects temperature_c as numeric, but an incoming feed renames it temperature_f and supplies strings. Predictions fail before scoring. What should be checked first?

choices.text: Retrain immediately on the malformed feed without inspecting it.
Interpret the failure as proof of concept drift.
Increase the classifier's regularization strength.
Validate column names, types, and units against the saved input contract.

questions.explanation: The observed problem directly indicates a schema and semantic mismatch at the input boundary. Validate and repair the contract violation before judging model quality or deciding whether retraining is appropriate.
questions.answerText: Validate column names, types, and units against the saved input contract.

questions.prompt: Tiny defects often occur along a 64 x 64 image's border. A 3 x 3, stride-1 convolution with valid padding shrinks the map. Which adjustment preserves the 64 x 64 spatial size?

choices.text: Increase stride to 2 while keeping valid padding.
Use fewer filters while keeping valid padding.
Replace the convolution with flattening and assume borders are preserved spatially.
Use same zero-padding with stride 1, while validating the effect of artificial border values.

questions.explanation: Same padding at stride 1 preserves the spatial dimensions and lets filters cover border positions with padding. It does not recreate missing real pixels outside the image, so border behavior still deserves inspection.
questions.answerText: Use same zero-padding with stride 1, while validating the effect of artificial border values.

questions.prompt: Select all actions that preserve an honest evaluation when preprocessing an initially unsplit labeled table.

choices.text: Fit a scaler on the complete table because it does not read labels.
Separate the held-out test data before fitting imputation statistics.
Use the held-out targets to decide which rows need different imputations.
Fit category vocabularies inside each training fold during model selection.
Apply the training-fitted transformations to validation data without refitting.

questions.explanation: Even transformations that ignore labels can learn information from held-out feature distributions. Split first, learn preprocessing within training folds, and reuse those fitted transformations on the corresponding validation data.
questions.answerText: Separate the held-out test data before fitting imputation statistics.; Fit category vocabularies inside each training fold during model selection.; Apply the training-fitted transformations to validation data without refitting.

questions.prompt: A safety-alert dataset has a rare positive class. Select all statements that support a careful evaluation.

choices.text: Macro-F1 gives each class equal weight when averaging class F1 scores.
Balanced accuracy averages recall across classes.
A high ROC-AUC guarantees that all deployed alerts will have high precision.
PR behavior helps inspect the trade-off between positive-class precision and recall.
Accuracy alone fully describes the model's ability to find rare positives.

questions.explanation: Balanced accuracy, macro-F1, and PR analysis reveal different aspects hidden by a majority-dominated accuracy score. The operating threshold, prevalence, and error costs still matter for deployment.
questions.answerText: Macro-F1 gives each class equal weight when averaging class F1 scores.; Balanced accuracy averages recall across classes.; PR behavior helps inspect the trade-off between positive-class precision and recall.

questions.prompt: Select all components that belong in a reproducible deployment package for a tabular classification pipeline.

choices.text: Only the classifier's final coefficient array, with unnamed columns.
A newly fitted encoder learned separately from each incoming request.
Version information and fixed reference inputs with expected predictions.
The fitted preprocessing steps and classifier together.
An input schema and recorded output/positive-class semantics.

questions.explanation: The fitted pipeline preserves the transformations the estimator expects. The surrounding contract, versions, and reference cases make it possible to validate that the reloaded system behaves as intended.
questions.answerText: Version information and fixed reference inputs with expected predictions.; The fitted preprocessing steps and classifier together.; An input schema and recorded output/positive-class semantics.

questions.prompt: Select all defensible interpretations after fitting K-Means to standardized sensor features without target labels.

choices.text: Including the known failure label among the input features is required for unsupervised evaluation.
Cluster 0 necessarily corresponds to the normal operating class.
The smallest inertia across all tried K proves the true number of physical operating modes.
Silhouette and cluster-size checks can complement inertia when comparing K.
A two-dimensional PCA plot can aid exploration but may hide structure in omitted dimensions.

questions.explanation: Projection plots and clustering scores provide evidence rather than ground-truth labels. Cluster identifiers are arbitrary, and inertia alone cannot establish the true number of real-world categories.
questions.answerText: Silhouette and cluster-size checks can complement inertia when comparing K.; A two-dimensional PCA plot can aid exploration but may hide structure in omitted dimensions.

questions.prompt: A deployed sensor classifier receives inputs whose range and missingness differ from its reference data. Select all justified responses before delayed labels become available.

choices.text: Record the alert and investigate its likely impact before choosing an intervention.
Conclude immediately that the conditional target relationship has changed.
Retrain automatically on the incoming values without checking their validity.
Check for unit changes, sensor replacements, and collection-pipeline faults.
Compare live ranges, null counts, and variances with reference summaries.

questions.explanation: Live distribution changes are investigation signals and can reflect faults or population shifts. They do not alone prove concept drift or establish that automatic retraining is the correct response.
questions.answerText: Record the alert and investigate its likely impact before choosing an intervention.; Check for unit changes, sensor replacements, and collection-pipeline faults.; Compare live ranges, null counts, and variances with reference summaries.

questions.prompt: A stratified random split automatically prevents both repeated-entity leakage and future-to-past leakage.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Stratification aims to preserve label proportions. Group separation and chronological constraints require additional design choices appropriate to the observation unit and deployment setting.

questions.prompt: The final test set can remain an honest one-time evaluation when the pipeline and operating threshold were selected using only training and validation evidence and then frozen.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Freezing the complete decision procedure before the final test prevents test results from guiding selection. Repeatedly changing it after inspecting test performance would weaken that separation.

questions.prompt: A scaler fitted on the training set should use those same fitted means and scales when transforming the held-out test set.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The fitted training statistics define the transformation expected by the model. Refitting on test data changes the transformation and lets the evaluation data influence the workflow.

questions.prompt: After MaxPooling downsamples an image feature map, every original activation can always be reconstructed exactly from the pooled output alone.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: MaxPooling retains only the maximum from each window and usually discards the other values. Downsampling can reduce computation and spatial detail, but it does not guarantee an invertible representation.

questions.prompt: For dilation 1 and stride 1, same padding preserves a Conv2D layer's input height and width, including when padding may need to be asymmetric for an even-sized kernel.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: At stride 1, same padding is chosen to retain the spatial size. An even kernel can require unequal padding on the two sides because the total padding needed is odd.

questions.prompt: Clearly separated colored groups on a two-component PCA plot prove that K-Means recovered the true supervised class labels.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: PCA is a projection, and clusters are algorithmic groupings rather than automatically verified classes. Apparent separation needs interpretation with additional evidence and any available external validation.

questions.prompt: A change in the distribution of input features can be covariate drift even when the relationship between those features and the target remains stable.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Covariate drift concerns changes in the input distribution. Concept drift concerns changes in the target relationship given inputs, so the two signals should not be treated as identical.

questions.prompt: When a pretrained feature extractor is kept frozen and only a new classification head is trained, the frozen extractor's weights are not updated by that training step.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Freezing excludes those weights from optimization while the trainable head adapts to the new task. Validation is still needed to determine whether the fixed features are useful.

questions.prompt: Comparing against DummyClassifier(strategy='most_frequent') helps reveal whether a classifier improves on always predicting the training set's majority class.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The most-frequent dummy provides a simple, reproducible reference using the majority class learned from training data. Beating it on accuracy alone still may not establish useful minority-class performance.

questions.prompt: Applying sigmoid independently to three logits guarantees that the resulting three numbers sum to 1.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Sigmoid maps each scalar independently into the interval from 0 to 1. It does not impose a sum-to-one constraint across multiple outputs.

questions.prompt: An output of 0.80 from predict_proba proves that exactly 80% of all future examples receiving that score will be positive, regardless of calibration or deployment shift.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A model's estimated probabilities are not automatically perfectly calibrated. Their empirical reliability must be evaluated, and changing deployment conditions can alter that reliability.

questions.prompt: For a higher-is-better score, the one-standard-error rule uses the best model's fold-score standard deviation itself as the tolerance, without accounting for the number of folds.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The rule uses a standard error of the best mean score, commonly estimated as fold standard deviation divided by the square root of the fold count. It then favors a simpler candidate within that tolerance.

questions.prompt: A category absent during training can always be added as a new one-hot column at inference without changing the trained model.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Adding a column changes the feature schema expected by the fitted estimator. Unknown categories need a predefined handling policy consistent with the training encoder and model.

questions.prompt: Responsible use of permitted AI assistance includes documenting its role, checking generated calculations or code, correcting errors, and retaining human accountability for the final decision.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Documentation and verification make assistance reviewable instead of treating generated output as unquestioned evidence. An accountable human still owns the final claims, corrections, and limitations.

questions.prompt: For a scalar input of -4, the ReLU activation outputs 0.

choices.text: True
False

questions.explanation: ReLU applies max(0, x) element by element. Negative values become zero, while positive values retain their magnitude.

questions.prompt: Complete the scikit-learn class name: from sklearn.preprocessing import ____ . This transformer centers numeric features and scales nonconstant features to unit variance using fitted statistics.
questions.explanation: StandardScaler learns the training means and scales. Keep its fitting inside the training pipeline so evaluation data do not influence those statistics.

questions.prompt: The categorical transformation that represents each nominal category using indicator columns is called ____ encoding.
questions.explanation: One-hot encoding creates category indicator features without assigning an artificial numeric order. The fitted category-to-column mapping must remain aligned during inference.

questions.prompt: Complete the method name to obtain a fitted classifier's class-probability estimates: probabilities = fitted_pipeline.____(X_new). Assume its final estimator supports probability prediction.
questions.explanation: predict_proba returns probability estimates in the estimator's class order. Check classes_ before selecting a column as the positive class, and do not assume perfect calibration.

questions.prompt: Complete the function name to save the entire fitted preprocessing-plus-classifier pipeline: joblib.____(fitted_pipeline, 'pipeline-v1.joblib').
